paper.title: Adaptation to the Range in $K$-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandits with bounded signed rewards and unknown range (model D_{-,+})
unmapped: Rewards are supported on an unknown bounded range [m,M] (signed); the learner does not know m nor M (scale-free regret); bounds scale with M-m
settings.definition_quote: For a given range $[m,M]$, where $m < M$ are two real numbers, not necessarily nonnegative, we denote by $\Dmod_{m, M}$ the set of probability distributions supported on $[m, M]$. Then, the model corresponding to distributions with a bounded but unknown range is the union of all such $\Dmod_{m, M}$

settings.name_in_paper: Oblivious adversarial bandits with unknown range [m,M]
unmapped: Rewards in an unknown range [m,M] (signed); the learner does not know m nor M; bounds scale with M-m
settings.definition_quote: a range $[m,M]$ is set by the environment, where $m,M$ are real numbers, not necessarily nonnegative. The player is unaware of $[m,M]$ and will remain so. The environment also picks beforehand a sequence $y_1,y_2,\ldots$ of reward vectors in $[m,M]^K$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandits with v-sub-Gaussian distributions (unknown v)

settings.name_in_paper: Oblivious adversarial bandits with known upper end M and unknown lower end m
unmapped: Rewards in [m,M]; the learner knows the upper end M but not the lower end m; bounds scale with M-m
settings.definition_quote: relying on an upper bound $M$ on the payoffs ensures that for all $m \in \R$ with $m \leq M$, for all oblivious individual sequences $y_1,y_2,\ldots$ in $[m,M]^K$

settings.name_in_paper: Oblivious adversarial linear bandits with finite action set and unknown range
unmapped: Payoffs x^T y_t lie in an unknown range [m,M] with m <= 0 <= M; the learner does not know m nor M
settings.definition_quote: A finite action set $\cA \subset \R^d$, of cardinality $K$, is given. ... there exists an interval $[m,M]$ such that ... $\dotptr{x}{y_t} \in [m,M]$. We assume that the player does not know in advance $m$ nor $M$.

algorithms.name: AHB (AdaHedge for K-armed Bandits with extra-exploration)
UCB with an increased exploration rate phi
AdaHedge for K-armed bandits with known upper bound M
AdaFTRL with 1/2-Tsallis entropy (known upper bound M)

symbols.Phi_free: scale-free distribution-free regret bound Phi_free(T) of the strategy, assumed o(T)

conditions: strategies adaptive to the unknown range with a scale-free distribution-free regret bound Phi_free(T) = o(T)
holds for all bandit problems in D_{-,+} (also for D_{m,+} with known lower end m)

source.label: thm:adaptive_lower_bound
source.quote: Any strategy with a scale-free distribution-free regret bound satisfying $\Phi_{\free}(T) = o(T)$ may only achieve distribution-dependent rates $\Phi_{\dep}$ for adaptation satisfying $\Phi_{\dep}(T) \geq T/\Phi_{\free}(T)$. More precisely, the regret of such a strategy is lower bounded as follows: for all $\nup$ in $\Dmod_{-,+}$, \liminf_{T \to \infty } \, \frac{R_T( \nup)}{T / \Phi_{\free(T)}} \geq \frac{1}{16} \sum_{a=1}^K \Delta_a

results.notes: Trade-off lower bound; algorithm class = strategies with scale-free distribution-free bound Phi_free = o(T). Remark 4 notes it also holds when lower end m is known.

source.label: th:adv_talpha_bound
source.quote: AdaHedge for $K$--armed bandits (Algorithm~\ref{alg:exp3_adahedge}) with a non-increasing extra-exploration sequence $(\gamma_t)_{t \geq 1}$ smaller than $1/2$ ... R_T(y_{1:T}) \leq 3 (M-m) \, \sqrt{KT \ln K} + 5 (M-m) \frac{K \ln K}{\gamma_T} + (M-m) \sum_{t = K+1}^T \gamma_t

results.notes: Generic bound for any non-increasing gamma_t <= 1/2. By the conversion in Sec 4.1, also a distribution-free bound for stochastic bandits.

symbols.a_AHB: exploration exponent alpha in (0,1) of AHB

tuning: gamma_t = min{1/2, sqrt(5(1-alpha) K log K)/t^alpha}, alpha in (0,1)

source.label: eq:defphiadvth2
source.quote: In particular, given a parameter $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, the extra-exploration $\gamma_t = \min \Bigl\{1/2, \, \sqrt{5(1-\alpha)K \log K} \big/ t^{\alpha} \Bigr\}$ leads to the scale-free adversarial regret bound \Phi_{\adv}(T) = \biggl( 3 + \frac{5}{\sqrt{1-\alpha}} \biggr) (M-m)\sqrt{K \ln K} \,\, T^{\max\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}} + 10 (M-m)K\ln K

tuning: alpha = 1/2, gamma_t = min{1/2, sqrt(2.5 K log K)/sqrt(t)}

source.label: th:adv_talpha_bound
source.quote: For $\alpha = 1/2$, the bound reads $\Phi_{\adv}(T) = 7(M-m) \sqrt{TK \ln K} + 10(M-m) K \log K$.

results.notes: Special case alpha=1/2 of r3, recorded since expression differs.

symbols.Phi_AHB: (3 + 5/sqrt(1-alpha)) sqrt(K ln K) T^alpha + 10 K ln K, the scale-free distribution-free bound of AHB

tuning: gamma_t = min{1/2, sqrt(5(1-alpha) K log K)/t^alpha}

source.label: th:adaptmorethanlog
source.quote:
For all distributions $
u_a \in \Dmod_{-,+}$ with expectation $\mu_a$, and all $\mu^\star > \mu_a$, we have \Kinf(
u_a,\mu^\star,\Dmod_{-,+}) = 0. As a consequence, all consistent strategies on $\Dmod_{-,+}$ are such that, for all bandit problems $
up$ in $\Dmod_{-,+}$ with at least one suboptimal arm~$a$, \liminf_{T 	o +\infty}  rac{R_T(
up)}{\ln T} = +\infty

results.notes: Regret is super-logarithmic; expression encoded as oo*log(T). Remark 12: also holds for D_{m,+}.

source.label: th:UCB-incr
source.quote:
UCB with an increased exploration rate given by a non-decreasing function $\varphi$ ensures that for all $v > 0$, for all distributions $
u_1,\ldots,
u_K$ that are $v$--sub-Gaussian, for all $T \geq K+1$, R_T(
up) \leq \sum_{a \in [K]: \Delta_a > 0}  rac{4}{\Delta_a} \varphi(T) + \sum_{a \in [K]} 2 \Delta_a \max \! \left\{  rac{32 v}{\Delta_a^2}, \, 1 ight\} \left( 1 + \sum_{t=K}^{T-1} \e^{- \varphi(t) / (2v)} ight)

results.notes: Algorithm from Lattimore (2017, Remark 8); finite-time bound is new. Whenever varphi >> ln, achieves distribution-dependent rate varphi adaptively to range.

R_T(y_{1:T}) \leq 12(M-m) \sqrt{d T \ln K} + 18(M-m) d \log K.

conditions: upper end M known to learner, m <= M unknown

source.label: thm:adv_any_exploration--simpler
source.quote: AdaHedge for $K$--armed bandits relying on an upper bound $M$ on the payoffs (Algorithm~\ref{algo:adahedgeM}) ensures that for all $m \in \R$ with $m \leq M$, for all oblivious individual sequences $y_1,y_2,\ldots$ in $[m,M]^K$, for all $T \geq 1$, R_T(y_{1:T}) \leq 2 (M-m)\sqrt{KT \log K} + 2(M-m).

results.notes: No extra-exploration needed when M known.

conditions: upper end M known to learner, m <= M unknown

source.label: thm:tsallis
source.quote: AdaFTRL with $1/2$--Tsallis entropy for $K$--armed bandits relying on an upper bound $M$ on the payoffs (Algorithm~\ref{alg:tsallis_ftrl}) ensures that for all $m \in \R$ with $m \leq M$, for all oblivious individual sequences $y_1,y_2,\ldots$ in $[m,M]^K$, for all $T \geq 1$, R_T(y_{1:T}) \leq 4 (M-m)\sqrt{KT} + 2(M-m).

results.notes: Minimax optimal order sqrt(KT) when M is known.

tuning: gamma_t = min{1/2, sqrt(5(1-alpha) K log K)/t^alpha}

source.label: th:adv_talpha_bound
source.quote: Theorems~\ref{th:adv_talpha_bound} and~\ref{thm:distrib-dependent} show in particular that AHB adapts to the unknown range, satisfies a scale-free distribution-free regret bound \Phi^{\AH}_{\free}(T) = \biggl( 3 + \frac{5}{\sqrt{1-\alpha}} \biggr) \sqrt{K \ln K} \,\, T^{\alpha} + 10 K\ln K

results.notes: Stochastic distribution-free consequence of Theorem 7 via the conversion of Section 4.1 (multiply by M-m).
